ppDatosGeoTxt: only when you turn it on, to show you where you are on the map, what is near you and the route to a place. It is not stored on any server. If you ask for a driving route, the start and end coordinates are sent to the routing service to work it out.
ppDatosCuentaTxt: email address and password. They are handled by
ppDatosRls: , which stores the password encrypted; we never see it.
ppDatosFavTxt: the identifiers of the places you save. With an account they sync; without one they stay on your device.
ppDatosPrefTxt: language, filters, active bus lines, cached weather and sea conditions, whether you have seen the tour, a visit counter, your answer to the cookie notice and, for the sky, the red light, the compass adjustment and the Wikipedia summaries of the objects you have already opened, the calendar reminders you mark and whether you have seen the compass guide. The events you add to your calendar (.ics) and the pictures you save or share are created on the phone and go straight to your calendar or to the system share sheet. All of this stays on your device and is not sent anywhere.
ppDatosPushTxt: if you turn them on, the subscription your browser creates — a delivery address and two keys — is stored, together with the app’s language, so the alert can reach you in your language. Turning them off in the browser stops it being used.
ppDatosSensoresTxt: only while you use “Point at the sky”: the compass, gyroscope and accelerometer say where you are pointing, to name what is in front of you. It is used on the device and is neither stored nor sent.
ppDatosCamaraTxt: only if you turn it on in “Point at the sky”, to draw the stars over the picture. The picture is not stored, not analysed and never leaves the phone; only if you tap 📸 is a capture composed with the stars over it, which is saved or shared from your phone without going through any server.
ppDatosStatsTxt: only on the website, and only if you accept them. See the next section.
ppStatsAntes: On the website, the app uses Google Analytics 4, and it is not loaded until you accept the cookie notice: until then nothing leaves the app towards Google.
ppStatsSi: If you accept, Google Analytics sets its own cookies and receives browsing data — screens viewed, language, approximate country, device type — and your IP address.
ppStatsConsent: It runs with Consent Mode v2 and the advertising signals stay denied at all times, so that data is not used to personalise ads. If you decline, nothing is loaded.
ppStatsGuarda: Your answer is kept on your device for 180 days; after that you are asked again. To change it sooner, clear the site data in your browser.
ppStatsTienda: The App Store app does not use Google Analytics: it never loads it and does not show the cookie notice.
ppPubQue: The map shows businesses that pay a monthly promotion plan. They are marked with the label «{patrocinado}» and do not alter the rest of the content.
ppPubNoDatos: That promotion does not use your data: everyone is shown the same ones, with no targeting, no profiling and no advertising cookies. There is no third-party ad network running in the app.
ppTercIntro: To work, the app requests data from outside services. They all receive your IP address and, in addition:
ppTercMapas: the map tiles, which is to say which area you are looking at.
ppTercOsrm: start and end points when you calculate a driving route.
ppTercNominatim: the text you type when searching for an address.
ppTercMeteo: the coordinates of the place or area whose forecast you are checking.
ppTercCarburantes: the official petrol station prices for the province, when you look at them; nothing of yours is sent to it.
ppTercWiki: the article title of the place or object you open.
ppTercGa: only on the website, if you accept the cookie notice.
ppTercNoVenta: None of this data is sold or passed on for commercial purposes.
